podcasts.title: Meta’s Muse: How we launched the most successful consumer product this year | Mona Sarantakos
podcasts.description:
Muse is the #1 app in the App Store and arguably the fastest-growing AI consumer product of all time. Mona Sarantakos has led product on it since day one. She’s VP of Product at Meta Superintelligence Labs and a 10-year Meta veteran with over 20 years of experience as a PM. This is her first podcast interview.

We discuss:

1. How a weekend with OpenClaw on a Raspberry Pi turned into Muse

2. Why Muse waited seven months to launch, despite getting started before most of its competitors

3. How Nat Friedman, Alex Wang, and Mark Zuckerberg each left their imprint on the product

4. How the team uses “agent swarms” to surface user insights at scale

5. The use case nobody on the team predicted

6. How Jolly, a placeholder avatar, became an icon

7. The two levers that actually move activation for an AI agent

8. The #1 thing Mona looks for in PMs today

—

WorkOS—Make your app enterprise-ready, with SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and more

podcasts.title: From Software Factories to Everything Factories
podcasts.description:
At SpaceX Super Intelligence, Lauren Tan and Roman Ugarte are on the core team that took Grok Bot from first line of code to launch in seven weeks.


It lets you spin up AI teammates with their own identities and logins, and they just keep working in the background. Their marketing team gave a bot its own ad budget. Lauren built an entire feature with her bot in one Slack thread without ever opening Cursor.


They joined us on the Lightcone to talk about what it’s actually like working next to bots every day, and how the hard part is shifting from doing the work to figuring out what to do and why.

podcasts.title: Nvidia After Jensen Huang, What Huang Meant to the AI Ecosystem, Washington Gets Its Revenge
podcasts.description: Ben and Andrew begin with a look back at what Jensen Huang meant to Nvidia, why AI changed the company, what Jensen’s efforts meant to the AI buildout, and what his absence could mean for both the AI ecosystem and the Nvidia F1 car. At the end: Celebrating 300 episodes of Sharp Tech with a nerdy chronicle of Ben’s journey into 3D printing, related AI show-and-tell adventures, and a Fable 5.2 triumph in Ben’s war with Mac mini permission dialogs.

podcasts.title: Alex Karp on Why AI Will Hurt the Middle Class: You Can’t Have Billionaires Becoming 100x Wealthier
podcasts.description:
To outsiders, Alex Karp seems an unlikely choice to lead Palantir. A philosopher by training, the billionaire co-founder has built his business at the intersection of intelligence, warfare and AI. To supporters, his software helps defend open societies. To critics, it gives governments troubling power to surveil and control.
In this interview, Karp tells Walter how dyslexia helped him bring together the impossible at Palantir, how Silicon Valley broke its contract with the rest of Americans, and why there needs to be a better way to re-distribute wealth. A conversation about national purpose, the Constitution and the trade-offs Karp is willing to make to keep the world safe.

Interview taped August 6, 2026.

ABOUT THE HOST
Walter Isaacson is the bestselling author of biographies of Elon Musk, Jennifer Doudna, Leonardo da Vinci, Steve Jobs, Benjamin Franklin, and Albert Einstein. He is a professor of history at Tulane University and previously served as CEO of the Aspen Institute, chair and CEO of CNN, and editor of Time. He was awarded the National Humanities Medal in 2023.

Alex Karp is the co-founder and CEO of Palantir. He co-wrote The Technological Republic and launched the sovereign AI movement.
